blocks.text: Ahead of Tuesday’s elections, party advertisements greet people arriving by train to the outskirts of the western Israeli city of Sderot. Campaign posters with various slogans promote the right-wing Likud and the far-right Otzma Yehudit parties. However, one poster is seen more than any others: that of the liberal Yashar party. Its slogan, “Rosh Memshala Dialna,” combines the terms “prime minister” in Hebrew and the words “of our own” in Moroccan Arabic. And there is a good reason why Eisenkot’s campaign in Sderot and other cities on Israel’s sociopolitical periphery focuses on his Moroccan roots. READ: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot […]...
